The verified fix, applied as a deliberate divergence. pager.ts checks whether the nav overflows in an afterRenderEffect that re-runs with previous()/next(), and through a ResizeObserver on the nav and its cells. API: POST /api/account/reset-password/check (Recovery/CheckResetTokenEndpoint.cs, operationId checkPasswordResetToken) answers 204, or AccountProblem.InvalidToken as ProblemDetails, and never uses up the token. It is mapped in the Accounts group next to the reset, with no AllowAnonymous. What makes a link valid (decode, then FindById, then VerifyUserTokenAsync) now lives in one place, ResetLinks, which ResetPasswordEndpoint reuses. Rate limit: its own 30-per-hour sliding policy per client address (ResetCheckRateLimit, added through Configure<RateLimiterOptions>), never PasswordReset. Three new tests in PasswordResetTests (a usable link, checked twice, then used; a damaged link, an empty token, another account's id; its own limit, with the forgot endpoint still accepted after it) all pass. residual: F2-07 trade-off, accepted: at 320 px /admin/monitoring is 344 px wide on the fixed branch, where the pre-fix branch (lodb-next, 18080) had no horizontal overflow on any admin page at 320. The cause is the unbreakable 'pg_total_relation_size' chip: h2 min-content 117 + gap 16 + chip 169 > head 235. The legacy overflows at exactly the same place (its chip ends at 344), and every legacy admin page is 466 px wide at 320. Measured options: min-w-0 on the h2 breaks 'FRÉQUENTATION' mid-word at 320. overflow-wrap:anywhere or min-w-0 on the chip, a percentage max-width on the chip, or flex-wrap with a flex-1 title each change the chip or title widths at 390 compared with the legacy. No simple rule keeps parity at 390 and removes the 24 px overflow at 320, so I left the fixer's layout as is.
